nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit through much of the year and feed bats, monkeys and apes. Their seeds are spread when animals eat the fruit.

nodes.name: Large-fruited forest trees
nodes.desc: Big-seeded trees such as wild mango depend on large animals to carry their seeds away. In the Cuvette Centrale many of them rely on forest elephants.

nodes.name: Marantaceae herbs
nodes.desc: Broad-leaved herbs that carpet openings in the forest understory and feed gorillas and elephants.

nodes.name: Understory shrubs and vines
nodes.desc: Shrubs and woody vines are staple foods for okapi, which browse leaves and buds of many such plants.

nodes.name: Riverbank grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses along rivers and swamp edges are grazed by hippos at night.

nodes.name: Straw-coloured fruit bat
nodes.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, flowers and nectar. It spreads seeds and is the main disperser of the African teak tree.

nodes.name: Red colobus monkeys
nodes.desc: Leaf-eating monkeys of the forest canopy. Chimpanzees and crowned eagles hunt them.

nodes.name: Chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Eats mostly fruit, but also fishes for termites with sticks and hunts monkeys and small antelope in groups.

nodes.name: Bonobo
nodes.desc: Mainly a fruit eater and the second-largest fruit eater in the Congo rainforest after elephants. It disperses seeds of many tree species and sometimes hunts duikers.

nodes.name: Western lowland gorilla
nodes.desc: Prefers ripe fruit but switches to leaves, herbs and bark when fruit is scarce. Spreads seeds in its dung.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and many fruits and carries seeds kilometres from the parent tree. Often called the megagardener of the forest.

nodes.name: Okapi
nodes.desc: A shy forest giraffe relative that browses leaves, buds, ferns and fruit in the understory. Its main natural predator is the leopard.

nodes.name: Forest duikers
nodes.desc: Small forest antelope that eat fruit and leaves and are common prey for leopards, golden cats, eagles and apes.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Break down dead wood and leaf litter and recycle nutrients. Chimpanzees fish them out of mounds with sticks.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Grazes grass on land at night and rests in water by day. Its dung moves land nutrients into rivers, where it feeds fish and invertebrates.

nodes.name: River fish
nodes.desc: River fish feed on invertebrates and organic matter and take up nutrients from hippo dung. Crocodiles eat them.

nodes.name: African golden cat
nodes.desc: A forest cat that hunts tree hyraxes and rodents, and also takes birds, small monkeys and duikers.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: Ambushes fish and animals at the water's edge, including hippo calves. Wikipedia notes crocodiles may threaten gorillas at Mbeli Bai.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: The main natural predator of okapi and a hunter of duikers and monkeys in the forest.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A powerful forest eagle that mostly takes monkeys, with duikers, bats and other small animals also on the menu.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong equatorial sun drives growth, but little of it reaches the forest floor.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: The Cuvette Centrale gets about 2,000 mm of rain a year, which keeps the forest and swamps wet.

nodes.name: Litter fungi and microbes
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil, but slowly in waterlogged peat.

nodes.name: Peatland soil
nodes.desc: Waterlogged swamp soils in the central basin store about 30 petagrams of carbon, roughly as much as all basin forests.

nodes.name: Seasonal flooding
nodes.desc: Rivers flood the swamp forests and riverbank grasses, spreading water and nutrients.
